identity.title: 3ViewSense: Spatial and Mental Perspective Reasoning from Orthographic Views in Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: Vision-Language Models struggle with elementary spatial tasks and with constructing coherent 3D representations from 2D observations.

gap.claim: The authors identify a missing view-consistent spatial interface as the bottleneck, rather than insufficient visual features or weak reasoning.

contributions.claim: Introduces 3ViewSense, which grounds spatial reasoning in orthographic views.
Proposes Simulate-and-Reason, decomposing complex scenes into canonical orthographic projections to address geometric ambiguities and support mental rotation and reconstruction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their framework by combining orthographic-view grounding with a Simulate-and-Reason mechanism for spatial reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant gains over existing baselines on spatial reasoning benchmarks, including occlusion-heavy counting and view-consistent spatial reasoning.
The authors report improved stability and consistency of spatial descriptions.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames a mismatch between strong language-model logic and weak Vision-Language Model performance on basic spatial tasks.
It describes a spatial intelligence gap and attributes the bottleneck to a missing view-consistent spatial interface.
It introduces 3ViewSense and its Simulate-and-Reason mechanism based on canonical orthographic projections.
The authors report benchmark gains and more stable, consistent spatial descriptions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a diagnosed representational interface bottleneck to a method that explicitly aligns egocentric perceptions with allocentric orthographic references.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make its method rationale more testable by connecting an explicitly diagnosed bottleneck to a corresponding intermediate representation.
lessons.application: When a task involves ambiguous 2D evidence and latent 3D structure, define the missing interface first, then design an intermediate representation that directly addresses it and evaluate the matching failure modes.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the task has no meaningful intermediate representation or when the diagnosis is not supported by targeted analysis.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark names, dataset sizes, metrics, baseline identities, or numerical gains.
The diagnostic analyses and the conditions under which the proposed interface outperforms alternatives are not described.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess the reported stability improvements or scalability claim.
